title: Why "the LORD is my shepherd"?
question: If the LORD is my shepherd, what does He actually do for me that means I shall not want?
blurb: David calls God his shepherd and lacks nothing. Trace what a shepherd does to see what that promise holds.

nodes.content: If the LORD is my shepherd, what does He actually do for me that means I shall not want?

nodes.verseText: A Psalm of David. The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want.
He makes me lie down in green pastures; He leads me beside quiet waters. He restores my soul; He guides me in the paths of righteousness for the sake of His name.
I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down His life for the sheep.
He tends His flock like a shepherd; He gathers the lambs in His arms and carries them close to His heart. He gently leads the nursing ewes.

nodes.content: "I shall not want" doesn't promise every wish, but that with the shepherd providing, the sheep lacks no needed thing.
